mechanism: Keep one compact identity board visible as a persistent verification anchor while the live evidence field changes through several environments. Each new field must prove a different behavior, scale or camera relation of the same subject; return to a readable board-plus-live-image composition often enough that variety never outruns identity.

invariants.rule: Keep one compact identity board or reference panel readable across the sequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without the anchor, the piece becomes an unrelated environment montage.

invariants.rule: Change the live evidence field at least three times while preserving one subject identity.
invariants.ablation_failure: Too little variation cannot prove transfer robustness.

invariants.rule: Give each environment a different proof role: action, scale, profile, close detail or interaction.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeating the same pose in new backgrounds adds no new evidence.

invariants.rule: Preserve face, silhouette and costume logic even when lighting and camera change.
invariants.ablation_failure: Identity drift defeats the verification task.

invariants.rule: End with both the stable anchor and one final live proof readable together.
invariants.ablation_failure: A decorative end card without live evidence cannot close the test.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.
